summary: Seiichiro Ono studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1914–1917). Working in Buddhist studies and other fields, he held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1951) and Aichi Gakuin University (~1960–1970).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Seiji Kimura studied at Komazawa University (~1977–1988). He later served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (~1990–1995) and held a post at Komazawa University (~1995).
Seiji Kumagai specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Kyoto University (~2003–2008) and became an associate professor there around 2017.
Seiji Nemoto, a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology, studied at Meiji University (~1968–1978). He later served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~2004–2014).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Seijun Ishii studied at Komazawa University (~1977–1986). He later served as a professor at Komazawa University (~2005).
Seijun Sato worked in the field of Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1951–1955) and later held a post at Taisho University (~1969–2003).
Seiko Hirata studied at Kyoto University (~1947–1950) and under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu (~1947–1953). Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he held a post at Hanazono University (~1953–1994).

Seiren Matsunami studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1927–1930) and under Walther Schubring (~1933–1936). In Indology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Taisho, Kyushu, and Rissho universities, and Chuo Koronsha.

Working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, Seishi Karashima studied at Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking universities under numerous supervisors. He held posts at Toho Gakuin, Eastern Institute, Soka University, and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology.
Seishin Kato studied at Toyo University (~1895–1899) and worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Toyo University and Taisho University (~1926–1943).
Seitatsu Matsunami specialized in Indology and Tibetology. He held a post as an assistant at the University of Tokyo in 1965 and served as a professor at Taisho University.
Seitetsu Moriyama earned his PhD at Bukkyo University and specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post in the Buddhist studies department at Bukkyo University from 1984 to 2013.

Seizan Yanagida studied at Hanazono University (~1939–1942). A scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, he held professorships at Hanazono University (1970) and Kyoto University (~1976–1985), and posts at the F.A.S. Society and Chubu University (~1985–1995).
Sen Wang studied at Peking University (~1932–1936). Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he served as a professor at Minzu University of China (~1952–1985).
Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Senarat Wijayasundara has served as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.
Senchu Murano studied at Rissho University (~1929–1933) and the University of Washington (~1935–1938). In the field of Buddhist studies, he later served as a professor at Rissho University.

A scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, Sengaku Maeda studied at the University of Tokyo, University of Pennsylvania, and University of Münster. He held posts at Pennsylvania, Tokyo, Gakushuin, Keio, and Musashino universities, and Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai.
Senkei Sakawa studied at Rissho University (~1960–1965). Working in Buddhist studies, he served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University in 1980.

Senmyo Naniwa earned a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1980–1986). In Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at the Eastern Institute and served as a professor at Bukkyo University (~1993–2013).
Working in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Sensho Hibi studied at Rissho University (~1955–1959). He later served as an assistant professor at Rissho University.
